pub struct Stack<T> {
    items: Vec<T>,
}

impl<T> Stack<T> {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Stack { items: Vec::new() }
    }

    pub fn push(&mut self, item: T) {
        self.items.push(item);
    }

    pub fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<T> {
        if self.items.is_empty() {
            None
        } else {
            Some(self.items.pop().unwrap())
        }
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.items.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.items.is_empty()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {

    #[test]
    fn lifo_order() {
        let mut s = Stack::new();
        s.push(1);
        s.push(2);
        s.push(3);
        assert_eq!(s.pop(), Some(3));
        assert_eq!(s.pop(), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(s.pop(), Some(1));
        assert_eq!(s.pop(), None);
    }

        assert_eq!(s.pop(), None);
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Version {
    pub major: u32,
    pub minor: u32,
    pub patch: u32,
}

pub fn parse_version(s: &str) -> Result<Version, String> {
    let parts: Vec<&str> = s.split('.').collect();
    if parts.len() != 3 {
        return Err(format!("expected 3 parts, got {}", parts.len()));
    }
    // Correct indices: 0 -> major, 1 -> minor, 2 -> patch
    let major: u32 = parts[0].parse().map_err(|e| format!("major: {}", e))?;
    let minor: u32 = parts[1].parse().map_err(|e| format!("minor: {}", e))?;
    let patch: u32 = parts[2].parse().map_err(|e| format!("patch: {}", e))?;
    Ok(Version { major, minor, patch })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn parses_simple() {
        assert_eq!(
            parse_version("1.2.3").unwrap(),
            Version { major: 1, minor: 2, patch: 3 }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_zeros() {
        assert_eq!(
            parse_version("0.0.0").unwrap(),
            Version { major: 0, minor: 0, patch: 0 }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_bad_input() {
        assert!(parse_version("1.2").is_err());
        assert!(parse_version("1.2.x").is_err());
    }
}

/// Find target in sorted slice. Returns Some(index) if found, None otherwise.
pub fn binary_search<T: Ord>(arr: &[T], target: &T) -> Option<usize> {
    let mut low = 0;
    let mut high = arr.len();
    while low < high {
        let mid = (low + high) / 2;
        match arr[mid].cmp(target) {
            std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => return Some(mid),
            std::cmp::Ordering::Less => low = mid + 1,
            std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => high = mid,
        }
    }
    None
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn finds_target() {
        let v = vec![1, 3, 5, 7, 9];
        assert_eq!(binary_search(&v, &5), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(binary_search(&v, &1), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(binary_search(&v, &9), Some(4));
    }

    #[test]
    fn returns_none_when_absent() {
        let v = vec![1, 3, 5, 7, 9];
        assert_eq!(binary_search(&v, &4), None);
        assert_eq!(binary_search(&v, &0), None);
        assert_eq!(binary_search(&v, &10), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_slice() {
        let v: Vec<i32> = vec![];
        assert_eq!(binary_search(&v, &5), None);
    }
}

/// Returns Some(index) if target is in the (sorted ascending) slice, else None.
pub fn binary_search(arr: &[i32], target: i32) -> Option<usize> {
    let mut lo: usize = 0;
    let mut hi: usize = arr.len();
    while lo < hi {
        let mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
        if arr[mid] == target {
            return Some(mid);
        } else if arr[mid] < target {
            lo = mid + 1;
        } else {
            hi = mid;
        }
    }
    None
}

#[cfg(test)]

        assert_eq!(binary_search(&v, 11), Some(5));
        assert_eq!(binary_search(&v, 7), Some(3));
        assert_eq!(binary_search(&v, 4), None);
        assert_eq!(binary_search(&v, 12), None);
        assert_eq!(binary_search(&[], 5), None);
    }

/// Merges two already-sorted ascending vectors into a single sorted vector.
/// Duplicates from both inputs are kept (so [1,2] + [2,3] -> [1,2,2,3]).
pub fn merge_sorted(a: &[i32], b: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(a.len() + b.len());
    let (mut i, mut j) = (0, 0);
    while i < a.len() && j < b.len() {
        if a[i] <= b[j] {
            out.push(a[i]);
            i += 1;
        } else {
            out.push(b[j]);
            j += 1;
        }
    }
    out.extend_from_slice(&a[i..]);
    out.extend_from_slice(&b[j..]);
    out
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_both_empty() {
        assert_eq!(merge_sorted(&[], &[]), []);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_one_empty() {
        assert_eq!(merge_sorted(&[1, 2], &[]), [1, 2]);
        assert_eq!(merge_sorted(&[], &[1, 2]), [1, 2]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_equal_length_non_empty() {
        assert_eq!(merge_sorted(&[1, 3, 5], &[2, 4, 6]), [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);

use std::collections::HashMap;

/// Parses a string like "foo=bar, baz= qux " into a HashMap.
/// Whitespace around keys and values is trimmed.
/// Returns Err if any pair is missing `=`.
pub fn parse_kv(s: &str) -> Result<HashMap<String, String>, String> {
    let mut out = HashMap::new();
    if s.trim().is_empty() {
        return Ok(out);
    }
    for pair in s.split(',') {
        let pair = pair.trim();
        let (k, v) = pair.split_once('=').ok_or_else(|| format!("missing '=' in pair: {}", pair))?;
        out.insert(k.trim().to_string(), v.trim().to_string());
    }
    Ok(out)
}

#[cfg(test)]

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_kv_normal() {
        let input = "a=1, b=2";

    }
